ns2:section.sectionText: Course Prerequisite: IE 410 or equivalent graduate stocahstic processes course. Over the last 100 years queueing theory has become a powerful tool for analysis and design of a wide range of engineering systems. Modern applications include: telecommunication, informaton and computing systems; network clouds; inventory control; service systems; and others. This course is an introduction to queueing systems and their applications in engineering. Topics include both classical single-stage models and queueing networks. Students will learn how to apply key ideas and methods of queueing theory, such as: Markov processes, embedded Markov chains, PASTA property, reversibility, product-form stationary distributions, stochasic stability, asymptotic analysis.
